I'm of the opinion that Reddit is here to stay, but it will increasingly become a place I don't want to go. A common belief seems to be that Reddit will suffer the same fate as Digg, however I don't think this will happen. Digg unilaterally alienated it's entire user community. Nobody liked the changes that were made, but what Reddit is doing is pleasing some users at the expense of others. There is a sizable, marketable, collection of people who like the idea of Reddit becoming a "Safe Place". Meanwhile, Voat will become the home of people who like the idea of a free market place of ideas, even ones they don't agree with. Both sites have a niche to fill and I think co-existence is better for everyone. If any site has something to worry about it's Tumblr. Despite how much Tumblr is mocked by people who don't agree with it's dominate culture, Tumblr does not nearly have the mechanisms in place that Reddit has for enforcing a a singular point of view. Once Reddit becomes the predominate "Safe Place" on the Internet, it seems logical to me that Tumblr users would migrate to Reddit as it will provide a larger "safer" community.
Reddit vs Voat end game - Annihilation or Two Site Solution?

Digg is still around. Somethingawful is still around. Hell, even Myspace is still around.

My bet is that Reddit's userbase will dwindle to almost nothing but I doubt they'll disappear for good.

We're almost in "if a tree falls in the woods and no one is there to hear it - does it make a sound? territory with those sites. If somebody just turned off Digg would it take seconds, hours, minutes or days before anyone noticed? They may not be dead, but they are so far removed from being relevant that they might as well be dead. My hypothesis is that Reddit won't suffer that fate, it's not in a death spiral it's just wrapping itself in a warm cocoon of "feelz" until it emerges a beautiful butter-fly that will make sure no one gets offended ever.
